objects.why: Stock and flow: water level, faucet inflow, drain outflow - bank balance, trust, oil.
The bounce is in the structure, not the hand.
Balancing loop; furnace vs heat leak; shifting dominance.
The cooling cup (balancing loop to room temperature) and the caffeine addiction trap.
Reinforcing loop: compound interest, rabbits, the industrial economy.
Capital -> output -> investment -> more capital; machines rust (depreciation).
The dealership's inventory swings; the tunnel gridlock.
The hotel shower delay: overshoot.
The fishing fleet that overshoots.
The renewable cod stock and its collapse threshold.
The non-renewable oil field - stock-limited.
The forest stock and the lumber mill.
Parameters - the weakest lever.
The paradigm - the strongest lever.
Behavior reveals purpose.
Personal debt; spend less = plug the drain.
Wealth that buys more wealth (success to the successful); budgets.
Monopoly: one player takes everything and the game ends.
Delays; waiting for flows to fill a stock.
Two competing loops; equilibrium.
Brittle hyper-efficient systems breaking.
One microchip factory losing power cascades through a supply chain.

spine.claim: The bounce is in the Slinky, not the hand: stubborn problems persist because of structure, not villains - a system is elements, interconnections and an invisible purpose read from behavior.
Stocks change only as fast as their flows, and feedback loops - balancing loops that seek a goal and reinforcing loops that feed on themselves - decide what a system does.
Delays make fast reactions overshoot, growth always meets a renewable or non-renewable limit, and only resilience, self-organization and serving hierarchies keep systems alive.
Systems fall into traps - success to the successful, shifting the burden, the commons - and we grab the weakest lever (numbers) while the strongest (goals, paradigms) sits untouched.
'It's the system' is no excuse: bounded rationality puts a heavier duty on each of us to widen what we care about, redesign the structure, and dance with systems we cannot control.

signatureObjects.name: The Slinky
signatureObjects.why: The metal coil spring toy held from the top and bouncing: the episode's opening and closing image - the bounce lives in the structure, not the hand.

signatureObjects.name: The Bathtub
signatureObjects.why: A bathtub with a running faucet and a drain: Meadows' stock-and-flow picture (water level = stock, faucet = inflow, drain = outflow), revisited for bank balances, oil and trust.

signatureObjects.name: The Thermostat
signatureObjects.why: The round wall thermostat behind the balancing-loop beats: furnace vs heat leak, shifting dominance.

signatureObjects.name: The Hotel Shower
signatureObjects.why: The shower head at the end of a long pipe: turning the dial to hot, getting scalded - delay causes overshoot.

signatureObjects.name: The Fishing Trawler
signatureObjects.why: The commercial fishing boat hauling nets in the North Atlantic - the fishery that overshoots and collapses.

signatureObjects.name: The Cod
signatureObjects.why: The fish population itself - the renewable, flow-limited stock that breeds, then collapses below its threshold.

signatureObjects.name: The Oil Pump
signatureObjects.why: The pumpjack on an oil field - the stock-limited, non-renewable resource that only counts down.

signatureObjects.name: The Factory
signatureObjects.why: The smokestack factory of the industrial economy - capital making output making more capital (reinforcing loop) while machines rust (depreciation).

signatureObjects.name: The Snowball
signatureObjects.why: A snowball rolling downhill and growing - the episode's image of a reinforcing loop / exponential growth.

signatureObjects.name: The Paradigm Lever
signatureObjects.why: The giant iron lever in the corner of the machine, labeled paradigm - the strongest leverage point nobody touches.

signatureObjects.name: The Tax-Rate Dial
signatureObjects.why: The tiny dial on the control panel the politician keeps twisting - parameters, the weakest leverage point.

signatureObjects.name: The Frog
signatureObjects.why: The frog that turns left and right to catch flies - behavior reveals purpose.
